purpose: Phase 6 eval: does the structural score separate resistant from neutral rpoB/rifampicin mutations?

resistant.labelSource: CARD (ARO:3003283), WHO-graded evidence - real catalogued resistance determinants, all single substitutions, all measured drug-contacting (<5 A) in this build's structural pipeline.

neutral.labelSource: PROXY negatives, not literature-confirmed susceptible phenotypes. CARD catalogues resistance determinants only - it has no confirmed-benign list, so no real negatives could be pulled from it. These were instead selected by an explicit, checkable rule: never reported at that residue in CARD despite rpoB being one of the most globally surveilled genes in bacteriology; structurally distant from the measured rifampicin pocket (>30 A vs ~3 A for the resistant set); high model confidence (pLDDT > 89); and a conservative substitution (same amino-acid class) so a resistance effect is doubly unlikely. This is a fair check that the tool measures what it claims to measure. It is NOT proof of generalization to a hard case such as a distal allosteric resistance mutation, and the separation this set shows should be reported with that caveat.

generalizationProbe.description: Phase 6's other eval: hide a known-resistant mutation from the catalogue lookup ('pretend novel') and confirm the structural score still flags it, while a pure catalogue lookup would return nothing.
generalizationProbe.rationale: Textbook case, drug-contacting at 2.71 A - if the structural score can't catch this when the catalogue is blinded, it can't catch anything.

knownFailure.description: A case this build is expected to get wrong, declared up front rather than left for someone else to find. The structural score only sees the binding site, so distal, allosteric and compensatory resistance is invisible to it. Reporting the separation above without this row would overstate what the method does.

entries.label: resistant
entries.why: 21 A from the rifampicin pose. No binding-site measurement can see this mechanism, so the structural read is wrong here and the catalogue is right.
